# Raindown

> Raindown is a superset of Markdown: a templating layer for static sites and an annotation framework for Markdown files. Directives add variables, loops, conditions, tables of contents, file lists, charts, HTTP examples and custom nodes. Content directives that are bare or in HTML comments write their output back into the Markdown file itself, so the file stays readable as plain Markdown by people and agents.

Raindown renders a `.md`, `.rd` or `.raindown` file to HTML, and on each render it may also rewrite the source file: filling in generated blocks (TOC lists, file lists, charts, endpoint responses, node output) and widening table columns. When editing a Raindown file, edit the directive, not the generated content between a written-back directive and its end, since that content is replaced on the next render.

## Rules for writing Raindown

- How a directive is written says what it does. `name:` opens a block and `:name` closes it.
  - Bare `toc:` (Raindown files only): writes its output into the file, and shows in bold in the HTML.
  - HTML comments, `<!-- toc: -->` ... `<!-- :toc -->`: writes its output into the file, and is left out of the HTML and GitHub's preview.
  - Deerheads, `<{ toc: }>` ... `<{ :toc }>`, or a self-closing `<{ :toc }>`: renders into the HTML only, writing nothing into the file.
- Template directives are always Deerheads, like `<{ if: draft }>` ... `<{ :if }>`, never bare.
- Variables are `{key}` (HTML-escaped) or `<{ key }>` (unescaped, so only for values you trust). Nested paths work: `{author.name}`. Unknown variables render nothing.
- Directives and variables inside inline code or code blocks are left as literal text.
- Arguments: an optional first value, then props written `key=value` or `key: value`. Values are quoted strings (`'notes'`), numbers, `true`, `false`, or unquoted variable names (`tags`, `author.name`). Quote literal strings, since unquoted words are variables.
- Template directives (`for:`, `if:`, `list:`, variables) are invisible in the HTML and may sit inside paragraphs, lists and tables.
- Content directives (`toc:`, `files:`, `chart:`, `endpoint:`, custom nodes) sit on their own lines with blank lines around them.
- Capitalised content directives are likely custom nodes. If there is a custom node in the .raindown folder of the same name then it's a custom class, if not it's just manually entered text.

## Bare directives (.rd and .raindown files, or raindown: true)

In a `.rd` or `.raindown` file (or a `.md` file with `raindown: true` in its front matter, or rendered with `--bare`), a content directive alone on its line needs no delimiters and no end tag. A bare block covers the Markdown block below it, up to the next blank line, and writes back:

```
:toc

chart: '3 5 2 8'
```

Use HTML comments and an end tag when the output spans blank lines. Comments and Deerheads work in every file type; bare syntax does not work in `.md` files without `raindown: true`. Template directives are never bare.

## Front matter and variables

YAML front matter holds the page's variables and metadata:

```md
---
title: Release notes
author:
  name: Mark
tags: [ruby, markdown]
draft: false
---

# {title}

By {author.name}

<{ for: tag in: tags }>
- {tag}
<{ :for }>

<{ if: draft }>
This is a draft.
<{ :if }>
```

Templates render before Markdown, like Liquid in Jekyll, so a loop's lines join into one list or table, and values may contain Markdown. `if:` tests truthiness; there is no `else`.

## Table of contents

- `<{ :toc }>` (bare: `:toc`): renders a TOC of the file's headings in the HTML only.
- `<!-- toc: -->` ... `<!-- :toc -->` (bare: `toc:` with the list directly below): also writes the TOC into the file as a nested list of `[Heading](#id)` links, regenerated on every render.

## Files and lists

Files in the project are listed by their metadata: front matter keys, plus underscored folders in the path. `docs/_basics/_1-getting-started.md` has `folder: basics`, `order: 1` and `path: docs/_basics/_1-getting-started.md`. Several folder tags in one segment are separated with `&`, like `_1&_basics`. A front matter list like `tags: [ruby, intro]` tags the file with each item. Files sort by `order`. The project root is the folder holding the `.raindown` folder, or else the rendered file's folder.

- `<!-- files: folder: 'notes' -->` ... `<!-- :files -->`: writes a link to each matching file, by title, into the Markdown and renders it as a list.
- `[[Note]]`, `[[Note#Heading]]` and `[[Note|text]]` render as links to the file named Note, anywhere in the project.
- `<{ list: page folder: 'notes' }>` ... `<{ :list }>`: repeats its template for each matching file, with the file bound to `page` (`{page.title}`). HTML only, nothing is written to the file.

Filter values must be quoted: `files: tags: 'intro'`.

## Charts

`<!-- chart: SOURCE ... -->` ... `<!-- :chart -->` draws data in block characters and writes it into the file as a code block, redrawn on every render.

- SOURCE: a CSV, TSV, JSON or YAML path relative to the project (`'data/sales.csv'`), inline numbers (`'3 5 -2 8'`), or a variable holding any of those, a list of numbers, or a hash of labels to values.
- `format:` `'bars'`, `'columns'`, `'line'` or `'sparkline'`. Default: bars for labeled data, sparkline for bare numbers.
- `label:` and `value:` name the columns to use. Default: first column for labels, first numeric column after it for values.
- `minus:` names a column charted against the values (left of the axis for bars, below it otherwise).
- `width:` (default 40) and `height:` (default 8).

## Tables

`table: 'data/team.csv'` writes a CSV or TSV file as a Markdown table, after `<!-- table ROWS rows · HASH -->`.

- Editing the table writes its rows back to the file, and editing the file writes the table again. HASH is of the rows when both last matched, so Raindown can tell which changed.
- When both changed, neither is written, and the comment reads `<!-- table conflict · HASH -->` until they match. Delete the comment, or empty the table, to keep the file's rows.

## Endpoints

`endpoint:` goes above a `curl` snippet in a fenced `sh` block. Raindown runs it and writes `<!-- response STATUS · DURATION · YYYY-MM-DD -->` below it, then the response in a code block, typed by content type.

````md
endpoint: status: 200 schema: Schema[uuid: String]
```sh
curl https://httpbin.org/uuid
```
<!-- response 200 · 142 ms · 2026-10-14 -->
```json
{ "uuid": "..." }
```
````

- The request runs only when the response block is missing or empty, and the CLI gets `-x` / `--execute`. Empty the response block to refresh it.
- Bare, in a `.rd` file, a Markdown file with `raindown: true` front matter, or with `--bare`, `endpoint:` holds the lines straight below it, its snippet, response comment and response, up to the next blank line.
- `{name}` in a snippet is filled from front matter, the `.raindown/environments.yml` environment (`--env NAME`), `{env.NAME}` environment variables, and earlier responses named with `as:`, like `endpoint: as: login` then `{login.token}`.
- Secrets go in `.raindown/environments.local.yml`, which git ignores. A response or error that echoes one of its values, or an `{env.NAME}` value, is written with the placeholder instead.
- `status:` and `schema:` check every response in the file, by the status in the comment above it. A schema is a LowType type written with `Schema[]`, not `{}`, like `Array[Schema[id: Integer, email: String | nil]]`. `--html` lists failures and exits with 1.
- `<!-- schema: User -->` names a schema for endpoints below it, from the indented `key: Type` lines after it, up to a line of `-->` (bare, up to the first line that isn't indented). A key with no type holds the more indented fields under it. Use it like `schema: User` or `schema: Array[User]`. Schemas in `.raindown/schemas.rd`, written bare, are shared by every file.
- Curl runs without a shell and without `~/.curlrc`: no pipes, redirects, `$VARIABLES`, `@file` values, or options like `-o`, `-F`, `-K`, or `-L` (redirects aren't followed). Link-local addresses, like cloud metadata at `169.254.169.254`, are refused.

## Custom nodes

Nodes are Ruby classes (LowNode subclasses) in a `.raindown/` folder at or above the file. `replace` returns Markdown written into the file; optional `render` returns HTML for the page.

```ruby
# .raindown/changelog.rb
class Changelog < LowNode
  def initialize(limit: 5)
    @releases = Release.all.first(limit)
  end

  def replace
    @releases.map { |r| "- **#{r.version}** #{r.summary}" }.join("\n")
  end
end
```

```md
<!-- Changelog: limit=3 -->
- **1.2.0** Bare directives close themselves
<!-- :Changelog -->
```

- Bare form: `Changelog: limit=3` with the output directly below, up to the next blank line (so the output can't contain blank lines).
- `<{ :Changelog }>`, a `<{ Changelog: }>` block, or bare `:Changelog` renders the HTML without writing to the file.
- A leading value (like `'data.csv'` in `chart: 'data.csv'`) is passed as the positional argument to `initialize`; props are keyword arguments.
- `replace` and `render` may accept the keywords `document:`, `metadata:` and `bare:`.
- A capitalized `Name:` only starts a node block if a loaded LowNode by that name has `replace`, so prose like `Note:` is safe.
- Built-in `toc:`, `files:` and `chart:` are nodes too, and can be overridden: `class TOC < Raindown::TOC`, `class Files < Raindown::Files`, `class Chart < Raindown::Chart`.

## Config

`.raindown/config.yml`:

```yaml
highlight_code: false   # no server-side highlighting; code gets class="language-x" instead
```

## CLI

```sh
raindown [PATH]               # browse a project's files and outlines in the terminal, writing back on save
raindown watch                # watch the projects (folders with .raindown) in the current directory, writing back on save
raindown watch DIRECTORY      # watch the projects in another directory, like ~/dev
raindown watch FILE           # watch one file, writing back to it on save
raindown FILE --html          # render to HTML once, to stdout
raindown FILE --html out.html # render to HTML once, to a file
cat FILE | raindown FILE --stdin   # render stdin to HTML, without rewriting FILE
raindown FILE --bare          # allow bare directives in a .md file
raindown FILE -x              # run endpoint snippets that have no response yet
```
